findings.reason: The first-pass reachability argument assumes a positive per-problem relative length increment, but the script does not enforce that condition, so a negative increment can reverse the gain sign, select a zero-correct group, and reach the branch that emits shortest-wrong-over-longer-wrong pairs.

The both-zero filter and accuracy margin guarantee a correct chosen group only when the relative length increment is positive, while an unenforced negative increment flips the gain sign and can leave an all-wrong group on the chosen side of the inter-group Cartesian product.
